find: solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short
title: Nasty, brutish, and short
note: Life without a common power to keep everyone in awe — Hobbes' reason for accepting almost any government.

find: Of Man’s first disobedience
title: Of Man's first disobedience
note: Milton states his subject and his aim: to justify the ways of God to men.

find: Better to reign in Hell, than serve in Heaven
title: Better to reign in Hell
note: Satan, newly defeated, decides what to make of the place he has been thrown into.

find: Commit it then to the flames
title: Commit it then to the flames
note: The closing paragraph, disposing of every book that survives neither mathematics nor experience.

find: How selfish soever man may be supposed
title: How selfish soever

find: led by an invisible hand to promote an end which was no part of his intention
title: The invisible hand
note: The phrase appears exactly once in the book, in a passage about preferring domestic industry.

find: the starry heavens above and the moral law within
title: The starry heavens and the moral law
note: Kant's conclusion, and the sentence carved on his grave.

find: If men were angels, no government would be necessary
title: If men were angels

find: A specter is haunting Europe
title: A spectre is haunting Europe

find: Call me Ishmael
title: Call me Ishmael

find: Over himself, over his own body and mind, the individual is sovereign

find: the legal subordination of one sex to the other
title: The legal subordination of one sex
